# Didache Chapter 5 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 5 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/DID_005_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 5

**1** The way of death is this: above all it is evil and full of a curse. Here are its people: murderers, adulterers, the lustful, the sexually immoral, thieves, idolaters, practitioners of magic, sorcerers, robbers, false witnesses, hypocrites, the deceitful, the crafty, the arrogant, the malicious, the self-willed, the greedy, the foul-mouthed, the jealous, the insolent, the proud, the boastful;

**2** persecutors of the good, haters of truth, lovers of falsehood, who do not acknowledge the reward of righteousness, who do not hold to what is good or to just judgment, who lie awake planning evil rather than good — from whom gentleness and patience are utterly absent — lovers of worthless things, chasers of reward, who have no compassion for the poor, who do not exert themselves for the burdened, who do not acknowledge their Creator, murderers of children, corruptors of what God has formed, who turn away from one who is in need, who crush the afflicted, advocates of the rich, lawless judges of the poor — sinners in every way. Children, may you be delivered from all of these.

---

*LOGOS notes: The "way of death" catalog is among the densest vice lists in early Christian literature. Its structure is intentionally overwhelming — the reader is meant to feel the weight of accumulated wickedness. "Corruptors of what God has formed" (φθορεῖς πλάσματος θεοῦ) alludes to the creation narrative (Gen 2:7, where God forms [πλάσσω] humanity from clay) — to corrupt another human is to corrupt God's own creative work. The final address "Children" closes the Two Ways teaching with pastoral urgency.*
